infra.help.title: No credentials yet?
infra.help.intro: The AWS CLI — and therefore AWOG — needs credentials it can use. An Account ID/alias + IAM username + password only works at the Console sign-in page, so it has to go through one of the two paths below.
infra.help.consoleBody: Close this dialog, then click Add profile → Console sign-in in the toolbar: AWOG opens a browser, you sign in with that same trio, done. No long-lived keys, no commands to type. (The terminal equivalent is aws login.)
infra.help.step1: Open the AWS sign-in page and sign in with Account ID/alias + IAM username + password.
infra.help.step2: Go to IAM → Users → your user → Security credentials tab.
infra.help.step3: Create access key → choose Command Line Interface (CLI).
infra.help.step4Csv: Download the *_accessKeys.csv file, then come back here and choose that file.
infra.help.step4Static: Download the *_accessKeys.csv file, then paste the Access key ID and Secret access key into the two fields above.
infra.help.blockedTitle: No Create access key button, or AccessDenied?
infra.help.blockedBody: Your organization blocks long-term keys. Ask an administrator for the IAM Identity Center start URL (then use Import → From SSO, the equivalent of aws configure sso in a terminal), or for the ARN of a role you are allowed to assume.
infra.help.passwordNote: AWOG never asks for the Console password, and the password never goes into ~/.aws — do not paste it here.
